claims: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has 160 to 2,000 km altitude.
Geostationary Orbit (GEO) is a circular orbit 35,786 km above Earth's equator.
Geostationary Orbit (GEO) allows satellites to stay over the same spot.
Perigee/Periapsis is the point in an orbit closest to the body being orbited.
Apogee/Apoapsis is the point in an orbit farthest from the body being orbited.
Polar Orbit is an orbit that passes over or near both poles.
Sun-Synchronous Orbit is a nearly polar orbit that passes over any given spot on Earth's surface at the same local solar time.
Gravity equation is F = G m1 m2 / r^2.
Orbital velocity is the square root of the gravitational constant times the central mass divided by the radius.
Early astronomers believed in geocentric models where everything orbited the Earth.
Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric (sun-centered) model.
Johannes Kepler determined that orbits were elliptical (not perfectly circular).
Isaac Newton later developed the physical laws explaining why objects orbit.
In 1962, John Glenn became the first American to enter Earth orbit.
In atomic models, electrons orbit the nucleus.
